title: ASDR: Exploiting Adaptive Sampling and Data Reuse for CIM-based Instant Neural Rendering
problem: Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) inference exhibits irregular memory access patterns and high computational overhead, making it unsuitable for low-latency, power-efficient deployment on edge devices. Standard compute architectures cannot bridge the gap between NeRF's memory-bound irregular accesses and the immediacy/power requirements of practical neural rendering.
motivation: NeRF-based neural rendering demands instant, power-efficient inference for practical AR/VR and mobile applications, but the combination of irregular access patterns and large MLP computations overwhelms conventional memory hierarchies.
method: ASDR performs neural rendering calculations directly in specialized memory chips (computing-in-memory arrays) rather than sending data back and forth to a processor, eliminating expensive transfers. It uses adaptive sampling to reduce computation by adjusting how many sample points to process per ray based on scene complexity, and data reuse to further cut computation by exploiting similarities in nearby rays and consecutive frames so the memory chip can reuse earlier calculations. Together, these techniques reduce both the number of operations and the energy required per operation.
key_novelty: The core innovation is combining adaptive ray sampling and data reuse techniques—specifically designed to work together on in-memory computation arrays—to simultaneously reduce the irregular memory access and total computation in neural rendering.
contributions: CIM-based accelerator mapping for NeRF inference targeting irregular memory access patterns
Adaptive sampling scheme that dynamically reduces per-ray sample counts
Data reuse strategy exploiting spatial/temporal coherence across rays and frames
Instant neural rendering with improved power efficiency over conventional compute platforms
baselines: existing mainstream neural rendering models on conventional hardware
limitations: Quantitative speedup and energy numbers are not reported in the abstract; applicability to dynamic scenes with low spatial coherence not discussed.
primary_theme: CIM-accelerated neural radiance field inference with adaptive sampling
